newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore makes key breakthrough in Internet trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore makes key breakthrough in Internet trade.

text.p: An international consortium in Singapore said it made a major breakthrough in secure Internet trade on Tuesday with what it called the world's first live sale using Secure Electronic Transaction (SET) standards.
"The stage is now set for secure electronic transactions on the Internet," said a statement from Visa International, the company issuing the credit card used for the purchase.
It said the world's first live cross border Internet sale cleared away a significant obstacle by using SET standards to link two different technology bases.

"In the physical world, the parallel would be like being able to use your Visa card only at one retailer or one group of retailers because the technology is not compatible elsewhere," said Dennis M. Goggin, Visa International President for Asia-Pacific.

"The inter-operability of today's transactions means that the SET standard takes care of something many of us take for granted -- that our method of payment is accepted around the globe, no matter who built the machinery or the technology that supports that payment," he addded.

The historic purchase saw Stephen Yeo, chief executive of Singapore's National Computer Board (NCB), use an electronic version of a Citibank Visa card to buy goods from two Singapore SET-certified retailers.
The Singapore transactions were followed by a sale at the same retail stores via the Internet with a Visa card issued in Taiwan.

Singapore set up its SET testing programme in September 1996 in conjunction with about 40 organisations including NCB, Visa, banks and merchants. It was one of 19 SET projects Visa was working on globally.

SET is set for further trials, with several thousand Visa cardholders from participating banks in Singapore expected to make secure Internet purchases from a range of local suppliers from the middle of 1997.
